## p159 A — Arad provisions and strength report: conditional partial recovery

**Edition context:** Arad provisions and reported strength: the restored copies.

<a id="edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial-arad-provisions-and-reported-strength-the-restored-copies"></a>

<a id="edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial-arad-provisions-and-strength-report-conditional-partial-recovery"></a>



**The second reception turns an uncertain strength field into an observed
80000 MANN.** The report addresses provisions, trains to Arad and an approach
to the Hungarian government; it also gives 30000 TIERE. Its two durations,
14 and 10 days, remain in the transmitted order without an invented
explanation of how they relate.

The p159 A source is damaged by repeated groups and missing coordinates.
The independently received [p168 E copy](168.md#edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-p168-e)
now supplies all eleven missing values and fixes the duration separator as
X, replacing the earlier optional U. The current source-linked reading has
**135 of 136 fixed labels under the published partial square**. The last
uncertainty in that layer is a shared footer cell,
not the strength figure.

**Source recovery and edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.
The unchanged Nov7–9 key is credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils
Kopal and Arno Wacker. Earlier OCR and the original reconstruction remain
attributed in their evidence packages.

<a id="edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 reference interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **6** in the footer, giving **RM 1C 186 GEH** and **136/136 conditional edited labels**. The opposite assignment gives 185 GEH. This adds no coordinate change or fill to the current seven-substitution collation. The pair is originally observed in all eight retained source maps; raw p159 still ends 186 GLH before the separately priced GEH repair.

<a id="edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial-what-can-be-read-and-under-which-model"></a>

### What can be read, and under which model

**Readable German — current p159 common reading; seven observed substitutions, source-supported fills, footer unresolved:**

> An OHL. Verpflegung noch 14 Tage. 10 Tage. Verpfleg. Zuege nach Arad. Arad bei ungar. Regierung erwirken. STAEKE 80000 Mann, 30000 Tiere. AOK11. RM 1C18?GEH.

The message asks for provision trains to Arad and for something to be
obtained through the Hungarian government. It records the military and
administrative work of sustaining movement: food, trains, permission and
reported manpower and animals appear in one compact telegram. It does not
establish that the trains arrived or independently authenticate the strength
as an actual headcount.

`STAEKE` stays as its six transmitted labels; no R is inserted. The repeated
`ARAD` and the separate 14-day/10-day statements are retained. The common
edited footer is `18?GEH`, with ?={5,6}; adopting the p168 E spelling in p159
costs one of the seven observed-coordinate substitutions. Raw p159 ends
`GLH`, and that disagreement remains in the source-linked stream below.

<summary>Current p159 source-linked and explicitly repaired streams</summary>

**Raw output — p159 primary geometry with all 11 missing coordinates supplied from observed p168 pairs:**


<a id="edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial-explicit-structural-cost"></a>

### Explicit structural cost

The copy supplies source evidence for the missing values; it does not erase
the reconstruction’s structural assumptions. The current collation uses
the same finite family of duplicated groups and gaps, now compared against
observed coordinates in the second reception.

| Operation in the current p159 collation | Count or result |
| --- | --- |
| Native p159 source | 271 observed coordinates; header advertises 272 |
| Exclude one copy of each repeated `VDAGG` and `FFXDF` | 10 observed coordinates |
| Add two five-slot gaps and one slot in `GDDA` | 11 slots; model length 272 |
| Supply those additions from directly observed p168 coordinates | All 11; no donation uses p168’s borrowed or missing values |
| Minimum source-to-source disagreement | 5 differences across 258 jointly observed comparisons |
| Retained source-origin maps | 8, all producing the same completed ciphertext |
| Common word proposal | 7 observed p159 substitutions; 135/136 fixed labels |

The source-only comparison examines 173,580 canonical layouts and 694,320
source-origin maps. The eight minima replace the earlier 64 word-conditioned
maps and remove their P0000 alternatives. This is a minimum within a declared
source-edit family, not proof of a unique historical transmission failure.
The [cross-copy certificate](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/certificates.json)
records every origin, price and both globally consistent footer assignments.

<a id="edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial-every-tied-source-map-is-retained"></a>

### Every tied source map is retained

The earlier text-conditioned search covered 173,580 canonical layouts and
694,320 source-origin maps: either instance of each duplicated group could
be excluded, a single slot was added around GDDA, and two five-slot gaps
were placed at the remaining boundaries. It retained 64 minimum source
maps at six observed-coordinate changes. Those old prices and every map
remain in the [original certificate](../../experiments/arad_provisions_partial/certificates.json).

The new coordinate-only comparison retains eight maps with one completed
stream. Its five-disagreement objective compares two sources, rather than
a supplied plaintext template; these are different costs, not competing
claims about the same repair count.

<a id="edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial-the-first-quantity-and-footer-stay-linked"></a>

### The first quantity and footer stay linked

Before the complete copy was inspected, the primary strength pair had domain
{3,4,5,6,8,P,V}. Sixteen word-minimum maps left it open; forty-eight produced
literal P0000 and filled all eleven additions. The latter display was:

**Conditional interpretation — one tied map retaining literal P0000; six substitutions and eleven added-slot fills:**

```text
ANOHLXVERPFLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEU10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXZUEGENACHARADXARADBEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKEP0000MANNX30000TIEREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX
```

These were alternative maps, not independent witnesses or votes for P.
The new observed p168 pairs fix 80000 and eliminate those P0000 alternatives
within the tested source family. Only the footer’s shared VF={5,6} choice
remains unresolved. The original twelve global completion witnesses and
map-specific compatibility records remain historical calculation evidence.

## p158 — Composite routing and key instructions

**Sources on this page:** p159 B, p159 C.

**Related source pages:** [p158](158.md#source-p158), [p168 D](168.md#source-p168-d).

<a id="edition-cases-p158-p158--composite-routing-and-key-instructions"></a>



The historical p158 D record combines portions of two routing instructions under the published **Nov7–9** key. We identified its prefix with p159 B and its suffix with p159 C; repeated transmissions on p168 C/D support the component readings and several source repairs.

<a id="source-p159-b"></a>
<a id="source-p159-c"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-p158-component-readings"></a>

### Component readings

The p159 B frame has a duplicated five-coordinate group, a missing group, two erased coordinates and a source disagreement. In p159 C, comparison with the repeat reduces a six-coordinate group to five. Three edited component versions re-encrypt exactly using the established square cells, with the digit pair 5/6 unresolved. The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p158.json) records the repairs and raw readings.

Sources: [p158 D](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p158_D.png), [p159 B/C](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p159_BC.png), [p168 C/D](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p168_CD.png).

<a id="edition-cases-p158-most-likely-component-readings"></a>

### Most likely component readings

**Component B, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bayr. Gen.-[Kdo.], [Muenchen], an 7. [unit unclear] Div., [Landsberg an/am Lech]. Nicht durch Kabel. Armeeschluessel [doppelt]. Empfang [bestaetigen]. O.H.L. […] 11338 geh. […]

**Component C, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bair. Gen.-Kmd., Muenchen, an 4. bair. Div., [Innsbruck]. Nicht durch [Kabel]. [Armee-CHI] doppelt. Empfang [bestaetigen]. An O.H.L. […]

In both displays, `[…]` omits damaged or unexpanded administrative fields.
The exact component witnesses below retain their labels and positions.

**Meaning:** Route messages through the Bavarian command in Munich, onward to the indicated formations or destinations. Do not use cable transmission; apply the specified army-key treatment and acknowledge receipt.

The place-name expansions, unit labels and administrative fields remain partly conjectural. `Doppelt` concerns the army-key instruction discussed in the historical report below.

| Source layer | Slots | Optimal split | Edit cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Typed text | 232 | 130 | 19 |
| Typed text plus handwritten groups | 242 | 130 | 24 |

The 242-slot alignment has 222 exact known-symbol matches. Exhaustive comparison gives a unique split at 130 in the prefix/suffix model, across all eight combinations of source layers and ambiguous glyphs. Treating both glyphs as unknown retains that split, at costs 17 and 22 for the typed and augmented layers. The resulting correspondence identifies the components; the cause of their combination remains unknown.

<a id="edition-cases-p158-earlier-historical-reading-of-a-component"></a>

### Earlier historical reading of a component

Childs's report dated **20 November 1918**, printed on p42 of *German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918* (1935), deciphers order **11338**. Its SY→RVV via N4 header, 9 November date and 21:03 time agree with the p168 retransmission. [Primary report, p42](https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/friedman-documents/publications/FOLDER_268/41784789082381.pdf).

The report expands the garbled destination as `LANDWEHR REGIMENT; AN FECH`. The coordinate-derived `LA3DSBERGXAN0LECH` more closely suggests Landsberg an/am Lech; the exact expansion remains editorial. The surrounding report describes a separate **double-transposition army cipher**. It does not establish two complete ADFGVX encipherments.

The component bodies on **p168 C and D** are also discussed by **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** in §6.4 of
[*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
printed p23 / author-PDF page 24. That credit also applies to the parallel p159 B/C bodies. Their gloss describes doubled confirmation; the raw text distinguishes the doubled army-key instruction from receipt acknowledgment.

The p158 composite identification and repair audit are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026**. The [historical comparison](../../data/reviews/historical_component_prior.json) records the earlier readings.

The [full p168 C witness](168.md#edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness) resolves the six-coordinate/four-coordinate group alignment. Its conditional frame fixes 139/140 raw positions, and an observed `V` from p159 B supplies the last coordinate. Twelve ownership aliases yield the same completed stream. The observed p168 pair `VG = K` also supports `GEN KDO`: adopting its G at p159 source 169 costs one `X→G` substitution, changing the H in `GEN HDO` above.

## p159 D — Kremp recovered and requests a departure date

**Edition context:** Kremp's request for a departure date — p131, p149 and p159.

**Related source pages:** [p131 B](131.md#source-p131-b), [p149 B](149.md#source-p149-b).

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-kremps-request-for-a-departure-date--p131-p149-and-p159"></a>



Kremp reports his recovery and asks the military mission's transport section to set his departure date. The unlettered final message on p159 reads completely under the published **Nov7–9** key: **98 positions, with no source correction**. Its different-key reception also repairs the earlier p131 B / p149 B version.

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-reading"></a>

### Reading

**Readable German:**

> Coeln 11. Ab. 1. S. Milmiss., Transp.-Abt. 1b, Constantinopel.
> Bin wiederhergestellt. Bitte Abfahrtstag bestimmen. Kremp.

**Meaning:** Kremp reports that he has recovered and asks the transport section
of the military mission in Constantinople to specify his departure date.
The opening `COELN11XAB1XSX` is directly decoded; its administrative meaning remains unknown. The displayed spacing and abbreviation breaks are editorial.

The complete p159 plaintext is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
COELN11XAB1XSXMILMISSTRANSPABT1BCONSTANTINOPELXBINWIEDERHERGESTELLTBITTEABFAHRTSTAGBESTIMMENXKREMP
```

</details>

All 196 source coordinates re-encrypt exactly using established square cells.

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-three-source-witnesses"></a>

### Three source witnesses

| Witness | Source heading and receipt | Key | Directly fixed positions |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| [p131 B](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p131_selected.png) | 5 November, continued; received 6 November at 02:36 | `Nov4-6` | 82/84 |
| [p149 B](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p149_selected.png) | 6 November, continued; received 7 November at 08:59; internal `0110 (6/11)` | `Nov4-6` | 84/84 |
| [p159, final unlettered item](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p159_selected.png) | 9 November; received at 06:12; internal `NR 17 (9/11)` | `Nov7-9` | 98/98 |

The last item follows a fresh **9 November** heading below the three messages
under 8 November. The machine-readable identifier `p159_D` is a local label
for the fourth item; the source itself does not print a `D` beside it.

The p131 and p149 ciphertexts differ at three slots: two p131 dashes correspond to p149 `A`s, and one `D` corresponds to `V`. The p159 reception uses a different transposition, square and address prefix. Its 51-character body matches **48 of 51** directly decoded characters in p149 and **45 of 51** in p131.

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-exact-repairs-to-the-earlier-version"></a>

### Exact repairs to the earlier version

The p149 source decodes literally as:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MILMISTRANSPABT1BKONSTANTINOPELXBINWIEDERHER4ESTELLTBITTEABFA7ETSTAGBESTIMMENXKREMPX
```

</details>

The independently readable p159 body supports `WIEDERHERGESTELLT` and
`ABFAHRTSTAG`. The resulting p149 reconstruction requires precisely three
changes to valid source coordinates, with no insertions or erasure fills:

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 134 | X | V | `4` becomes `G` in `WIEDERHERGESTELLT`. |
| 26 | D | G | `7` becomes `H` in `ABFAHRTSTAG`. |
| 106 | F | V | The following `E` becomes `R`. |

The remaining **165 printed coordinates** and the earlier address forms `MILMIS` and `KONSTANTINOPEL` are retained. The 84-position reconstruction re-encrypts to this three-change witness.

For p131, the same body additionally fills its two dashes and changes source
index 145 from `D` to `V`, yielding `BITTE` followed by `ABFAHRTSTAG`.
Its complete repair cost is **four known-coordinate substitutions and two erasure fills**.
